sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Cross-Border Reverse Logistics and Returned Goods Quality Grading

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Panama (Unitary National Jurisdiction; No Sub-State Tax Distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (with Anglocentric commercial-law influences in foundation, trust, and corporate statutes)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: United States–Panama Trade Promotion Agreement (TPA, in force 31 October 2012)
United Kingdom–Panama Bilateral Investment Treaty (1985, continued post-Brexit)
Panama–Mexico Tax Information Exchange Agreement; limited DTA network with South Korea, Singapore, and Spain under territorial-tax framework

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 25 of 12 June 1995 (Private Interest Foundations, as amended by Law 63 of 2009); Law 23 of 27 April 2015 (AML/CFT regime) as amended by Law 70 of 2 October 2019; Executive Decree No. 480 of 2019 (Beneficial Owner Registry); Registro Público de Panamá rules on UBO filing and mandatory electronic submission

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the Founder's passport or national identity card
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport office / civil registry of country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Panama acceded 28 May 1991; in force 30 July 1991); consular legalization only for non-Hague-state documents

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original Certificate of Good Standing (for any corporate founder or corporate Foundation Council member)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry of the founder's jurisdiction of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney authorizing the Panamanian registered agent to incorporate the PIF and appoint the Foundation Council
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public of the founder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds declaration for the initial foundation endowment
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized and countersigned by the Panamanian registered agent (internal AML KYC file)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP, OFAC, UN, EU, and Panama Consolidated List screening of the founder, Foundation Council members, and any protector; risk-based enhanced due diligence with beneficial-ownership verification to a 10% threshold; ongoing transaction monitoring under Law 23 of 2015, Article 24, and FATF Recommendation 12.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá – Electronic Portal (SEDE ELECTRÓNICA / PANATRÁMITE) foundation name search and reservation module
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Foundation names may be in any language using Latin-alphabet characters; if a non-Latin script is used, an official transliteration or translation must be filed; the statutory token 'FUNDACIÓN' or 'FOUNDATION' is mandatory, with 'Fdn.' accepted by prevailing registry practice.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Terms suggesting government or state affiliation (e.g., 'Gobierno', 'Nacional', 'Banco Nacional', 'Ministerio')
Terms requiring prior ministerial or regulator approval (e.g., 'Banco', 'Seguros', 'Fondo de Inversión', 'Trust', 'Financiera', 'Reaseguro')
Names identical, phonetically equivalent, or confusingly similar to an existing registered entity or recognized international mark
Words contrary to public order, morality, or religious denominations without authorization
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon registry rejection, the registered agent may file a written reconsideration petition (recurso de reconsideración) within 8 working days and thereafter a hierarchical appeal (recurso de apelación) to the Dirección General del Registro Público within 30 days; a fresh name-search may also be submitted in parallel.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted — a Panamanian licensed law firm or registered agent may serve as resident agent with a registered office address; for reverse-logistics PIFs operating exclusively abroad, a physical local office is not legally required, provided the statutory minimum endowment is deposited and the resident agent maintains the registered office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low; estimated 3% annual probability of unannounced physical on-site inspection for a standard Low_Risk_Standard PIF with non-resident operations and zero in-country physical footprint.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registry name search and clearance fee
Drafting of Private Interest Foundation charter (Fundación)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Panamanian licensed law firm / registered agent

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of foundation charter and ancillary documents
Registration and inscription fee at the Public Registry
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff calculated on foundation endowment

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered agent annual fee (first year, inclusive of pre-incorporation services)
Apostille of founder documents (3 documents at USD 40 each)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent authority of country of origin (Ministry of Foreign Affairs)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory apostille fee per Hague Convention certificate

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO declaration filing under Law 70 of 2019 and Executive Decree 480 of 2019
PEP / OFAC / UN sanctions screening and AML KYC compliance fee
Certified translation / transliteration of charter (if required)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (Private Interest Foundations), as amended; Articles 3-5 and 8-10 governing constitution, object, registered agent, and Foundation Council
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado (Public Registry of Panama, Private Interest Foundations Section)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución de Fundación de Interés Privado (Notarized public deed of incorporation)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum statutory founding patrimony of US$10,000, to be contributed by the founder and certified in the Escritura Pública; Panama does not require escrow with a licensed bank for PIF registration, but the notary must attest receipt or commitment of the initial assets.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Foundation acknowledges receipt of the founder’s contribution of US$10,000 as the initial patrimony, and that the proposed capital schedule is approved. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the Foundation shall be [address], Panama, and that [Registered Agent name] is appointed as resident agent. RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name] is appointed as President and Council Secretary, with full authority to open bank accounts, execute logistics agreements, and file all statutory returns. RESOLVED FINALLY, that the Foundation adopts the quorum and voting rules contained in the foundation charter, and that all acts performed by officers in furtherance of the Foundation's reverse-logistics purpose are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Notarize Foundation Charter (Escritura Pública)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría Pública de Circuito de Panamá (Civil Circuit Notary, Panama City)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct a Panamanian notary to prepare and execute the foundation charter containing the foundation name, registered office in Panama, initial patrimony of at least US$10,000, registered agent, and Foundation Council. Founder and Registered Agent must appear before the notary with identification; the notary will swear the instrument and issue the original Escritura Pública.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of founder's passport or identity card
Statement of initial patrimony and source of funds
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If notarial corrections are requested, amend the draft and re-execute before the same notary without affecting the proposed registration date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscribe Foundation Charter at Panamá’s Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado (online Sede Electrónica and physical counter)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized Escritura Pública to the Foundations Section, pay the official registration fee, and request inscription in the Foundations Registry. If using Sede Electrónica, attach scanned deed and fee payment voucher. After review, the registrar assigns a folio number and returns the inscribed testimony.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a 'requerimiento' (query), file a corrected supplementary document within 30 calendar days; failure to cure results in loss of filing priority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Certified Registry Extract and Foundation Council Appointment Record
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Certificates Section (or Sede Electrónica)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Request a certified copy of the inscribed Escritura Pública and a Certificate of Registration (Certificado de Registro). Simultaneously record the initial Foundation Council appointment in the same dossier if not already recorded, providing officers' identification and acceptance records.
required_dossiers: Payment for certified copies and registration certificate
Foundation Council appointment instrument and officer acceptance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is incomplete, request a corrective note from the Foundations Section or re-issue with the correct folio data.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for Tax Identification Number (RUC) with DGI
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas – Sede Electrónica
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the taxpayer registration form declaring the foundation's purpose, ISIC code 5229 (reverse logistics), registered office, and Foundation Council. Attach the Public Registry certificate and registered agent details. The system issues a preliminary RUC before the definitive certificate is produced.
required_dossiers: RUC registration form (Formulario de Registro Único de Contribuyentes)
Registered office lease or notarial domicile declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DGI queries financial capacity or address, submit a bank certification or amended lease within 15 business days to reactivate the application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Municipal Operation Notice and Occupational/Fire Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipio de Panamá – Dirección de Rentas Municipales and Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File an Aviso de Operación with the municipality listing warehouse operations for returned merchandise quality grading and storage. Schedule a fire-safety inspection of the physical premises and obtain the occupancy/fire certificate. If employees are hired, register with the Caja de Seguro Social.
required_dossiers: Building floor plan and occupancy certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipal inspection identifies deficiencies, remedy structural or fire-protection issues and resubmit inspection reports within 15 calendar days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) – Dirección de Normas y Tecnología Industrial (administering voluntary technical standards; no industrial license imposed for ISIC 5229)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No statutory industrial operating license for cross-border reverse logistics; optional Municipal Aviso de Operación and fire-safety certificate

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) – Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Category 1 Registration for indoor warehousing and quality-grading without industrial processing; no full EIA required
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Panamanian solid-waste management regulations; zero industrial wastewater discharge from sorting and grading activities; packaging and returned goods disposed or recycled only through licensed waste carriers; any potential VOC emissions restricted to non-industrial, naturally ventilated operations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá certificate confirming fire-safety compliance; structural load inspection of racking and storage areas by municipal engineer; MITRADEL occupational health and safety clearance for covered staff.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas, Panama; online taxpayer portal SIA (Sistema Integrado de Atención al Contribuyente) / e-Tax platform (efactura.dgi.gob.pa)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Private Interest Foundation (PIF) must first be duly registered with the Public Registry of Panama through a licensed resident agent. To obtain a RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente), the PIF must submit its foundation charter, the resident agent's notarized acceptance, identification documents of the founders and initial officers, registered address in Panama, and evidence of compliance with minimum capital requirements. The application is filed electronically through the DGI's SIA portal or in-person at a DGI attention center; a provisional or definitive RUC is issued upon verification, and the PIF is then enrolled in the national tax registry for ITBMS and income tax administrative purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not operate a check-the-box regime or allow hybrid mismatch planning for PIFs. A Private Interest Foundation is a hybrid-risk entity treated as a separate taxpayer for domestic tax purposes but only taxed on Panama-source income; no pass-through election is available. A PIF may, however, elect into the simplified ITBMS regime (Small Taxpayer Regime) if its gross taxable turnover falls below the statutory threshold and may voluntarily register for ITBMS even when not legally required; foreign-tax-credit elections are unavailable in the absence of a tax treaty credit mechanism.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (ITBMS) – VAT equivalent
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: PAB 36,000 (Panamanian Balboa) annual gross turnover for the simplified small-taxpayer regime; any person engaged in taxable transfers of goods or services in Panama is generally required to register and apply ITBMS unless expressly exempt, and non-resident suppliers providing services used or exploited in Panama trigger VAT registration when liable for collection
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama mandates electronic invoicing through the DGI e-Factura system. Taxpayers must obtain an electronic authorization code (Código de Autorización Electrónico, CAE) from the DGI before issuing invoices. Invoicing software must comply with the official XML scheme and digital certificate requirements; full real-time per-transaction clearance to the tax authority is not yet implemented, but periodic transmission/listing of electronic invoices is required under the phased mandatory rollout. Digital stamping of fiscal invoices is also required for certain legacy printers. The system applies to ITBMS-registered taxpayers including PIFs undertaking commercial transactions in Panama.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (0% ITBMS) applies to the export of tangible goods from Panama, including goods re-exported after being received through a return-merchandise reverse-logistics operation, provided title passes to a foreign buyer and the goods are physically removed from Panamanian customs territory within the legally permitted time. Also eligible are services rendered to non-residents and effectively used or exploited outside Panama, and services directly related to exported goods, subject to supporting evidence. Reverse logistics activities involving quality grading, repair, reconditioning, or consolidation of returned merchandise are eligible only if the services are expressly undertaken for and delivered to a foreign principal and the end-user/consumption occurs abroad; the zero-rated status must be documented at the time of invoicing.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración Única Aduanera / DUA) demonstrating exit from Panama's customs jurisdiction
Bill of Lading (original or verified electronic equivalent) issued by the ocean or air carrier evidencing shipment of the returned merchandise to the foreign destination
Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificado de Ingreso de Divisas) issued by a Panamanian bank or licensed exchange house evidencing receipt of the export proceeds from abroad
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGI rigorously audits export zero-rating claims, particularly cross-border reverse-logistics flows, to prevent fictitious exports or re-export schemes. A false zero-rating claim triggers the collector's demand for the omitted ITBMS (7%) plus monthly interest and late-payment surcharges, and fines ranging from 100% to 200% of the omitted tax under the Panama Tax Code. Knowingly issuing a fraudulent zero-rated export invoice may be prosecuted as tax fraud, leading to criminal penalties including imprisonment, disqualification from tax registration, and cancellation or suspension of the PIF's RUC. The DGI may retroactively reassess within five years for ordinary deficiencies and up to ten years in cases of fraud or omitted declarations; export documentation must be retained and produced on demand to avoid a full clawback of zero-rated treatment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: None. The Republic of Panama has no central bank. Banking supervision is vested in the Superintendency of Banks of Panama (Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá), while the Financial Analysis Unit (UAF) administers AML/CFT obligations for financial intermediaries. Foreign exchange matters fall under the Ministry of Economy and Finance only for customs and statistical reporting, not for exchange controls.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama is a fully dollarized economy: the US dollar is legal tender, and the Balboa is only a fractional unit with no independent monetary issuance. There is no exchange control regime and no differentiation between current and capital account transactions. Capital injections, dividends, interest, fees, and profit remittances may be freely made in USD through licensed banks. The sole practical constraints are bank-level AML/KYC requirements, contractual documentation, and adherence to Panamanian territorial taxation rules on Panamanian-source income.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export-proceeds surrender obligation, mandatory conversion ratio, or repatriation timeline applies in Panama. Exporters retain USD and may allocate proceeds without central bank approval. For banking and customs purposes, trade documents (customs declarations, invoices, bills of lading/air waybills, goods grading certificates) must be retained, but they are not used for exchange-control-based surrender requirements.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: USD Operating Account with Escrow sub-ledger capacity

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Medium and only as an ancillary payment-rail connector. An unlicensed offshore digital EMI may not offer banking or money transmission services to or from a Panamanian PIF without a banking licence under Decree-Law 9 of 1998, Article 4. Airwallex does not currently maintain a Panamanian banking licence and therefore cannot serve as the primary treasury node. The PIF must hold its main USD clearing account at a Panamanian licensed bank, using the EMI exclusively for cross-border reverse-logistics refunds to counterparties outside Panama where legal designation of the EMI as a collection and disbursement agent is permissible and not deemed prohibited Panamanian money transmission.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical appearance is mandatory for the principal foundation council member, the founder where identifiable, and any senior beneficiary conducting treasury operations. Remote onboarding is unavailable for new non-resident, foreign-owned PIFs without an existing Panamanian banking relationship. Superintendency Board Agreement 01-2013 and Law 12 of 1995 require a face-to-face interview for enhanced due diligence and beneficial owner verification; video interviews may supplement but cannot replace the in-person appearance. Some banks permit video for co-signatories and professional intermediaries, but the cornerstone applicant must appear physically in Panama or at a Panamanian diplomatic mission, subject to acceptable notarization.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PIF treated as an opaque hybrid vehicle with nominee council members and undisclosed beneficiaries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled original foundation deed and by-laws; Public Registry certificate of foundation registration; notarized council resolution appointing officers and signatories; a notarized, dated legal opinion identifying the economic settlor, protector if any, and enumerated beneficiaries; source-of-capital statements for the initial endowment; and independently audited financial statements or an opening balance sheet evidencing legitimate funding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume cross-border reverse-logistics fund movements involving third-party grading agents, carriers, and refund processors.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete commercial contract file comprising return-authorization agreements, reverse-logistics processing contracts, logistics service agreements, insurance certificates, customs declarations (SIICEX/DIUE), supplier invoices, receiving and grading reports, bank records identifying each payment, an organizational chart, and know-your-counterparty due diligence files on every participant in the return supply chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owners or trade counterparties presenting sanctions or politically exposed persons (PEP) risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Superintendency-compliant Onboarding and Enhanced Due Diligence forms, PEP questionnaires, sanctions/PEP database screening results, source-of-wealth evidence for each politically exposed or high-risk beneficiary, title or sale instruments, personal bank statements, sworn declarations of source of wealth, and a written undertaking to disclose changes in beneficial ownership on an ongoing basis.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid interbank USD movements into Panama without observable economic substance or coherent reverse-logistics operating model.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Panamanian office lease, employment agreements for local staff, board minutes approving treasury and clearing policies, a detailed business plan for goods return and quality-grading operations, monthly bank reconciliations, cash-flow forecasts, and, where applicable, an economic substance filing or professional opinion confirming that treasury operations are performed through and from Panama.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound capital injections must route in US dollars via SWIFT MT103 or Fedwire to the PIF's licensed Panamanian bank account. Panama imposes no exchange-control purpose codes or central bank registration; however, banks apply their own underwriting and OFAC-facing controls. The MT103 field 70 should explicitly state the purpose, e.g. 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION — PRIVATE INTEREST FOUNDATION'. The initial injection must be accompanied by a notarized foundation resolution authorising receipt, the foundation charter, and a source-of-funds declaration from the remitter. Funds from non-USD-sending jurisdictions may be converted by the sending bank, with the remitter's bank confirming lawful conversion and adherence to its own capital controls.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound reverse-logistics settlements are cleared primarily through SWIFT MT103 wire transfers from the Panamanian account to beneficiary banks. High-value or contractually structured transactions may use an irrevocable commercial Letter of Credit (UCP600) issued or confirmed by a Panamanian bank. Local USD clearing is available through Panamá ACH, which operates on a same-day or next-day cycle among domestic licensed banks. For mass return-refund payouts to non-Panamanian beneficiaries, the PIF may use an ancillary Airwallex virtual account only if the receiving party lawfully accepts such EMI payments and the Panamanian prime bank retains visibility of the transaction underlying invoice, return authorisation, and goods-received/quality-grade evidence. All disbursements must reference the return authorization number or commercial invoice, and the corresponding logistics and grading records must be available on demand.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Non-deliverable forwards for Latin American restricted currencies (CLP, BRL, PEN)
Cross-currency swaps for multi-currency treasury structures

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Private Interest Foundation Government Fee (Tasa Única Anual de Fundaciones de Interés Privado)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas, through Banco Nacional de Panamá; registry status reflected in the Fundaciones section of the Registro Público de Panamá
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 30 June; for a newly constituted foundation the first fee is paid at registration and the next annuity becomes due on the following 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment after 30 June triggers a 10% surcharge plus statutory monthly interest; three consecutive years of non-payment authorises administrative strike-off or dissolution by the Public Registry

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered Agent and Registered Office Continuity Maintenance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Foundation Registry; day-to-day records held by the licensed resident agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Continuous obligation; any resignation, replacement, or address change must be registered within 30 days of the triggering event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Loss of a licensed resident agent may trigger registry suspension; prolonged absence of an agent is a ground for administrative strike-off of the foundation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership and Foundation Council Confirmation for AML Compliance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Compliance unit of the licensed resident agent; not a public filing but subject to inspection by the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 January of each calendar year, or within 15 days of any change in foundation council composition, protector, beneficiaries, or beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance exposes the foundation and the resident agent to monetary penalties under Law 23 of 2015, as amended, and may lead to suspension of the foundation's registry standing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Income Tax Situation Filing for Panamanian-Source Income or Formal Non-Filing Status
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 30 March following a 31 December fiscal year-end; entities with a different accounting close must file by the anniversary of the closing date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs a 10% surcharge on tax due plus 1% monthly interest; continued default can result in enforced collection proceedings and attachment of Panamanian banking assets

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory independent audit is required under Law 25 of 1995 solely for being a Private Interest Foundation. A certified audit becomes compulsory if the foundation is designated a 'contribuyente global relevante' by the DGI, generally where annual gross revenue from Panamanian-source activities or total assets exceed USD 3,000,000, or if required by the foundation's governing instrument, creditors, or applicable counterparty arrangements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Panama applies IFRS as localised by the Colegio de Contadores Públicos de Panamá; large taxpayers subject to DGI audit must use full IFRS, while smaller non-reporting PIFs may apply IFRS for SMEs. Books and records must be expressed in balboas/USD, maintained at least in Spanish, and prepared in accordance with the chart of accounts regime accepted by the DGI.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: A PIF has no share capital and no shareholders, so no annual shareholding-transfer confirmation applies. Instead, the foundation council must annually confirm to the resident agent the identities of the founder, council members, protector, and beneficiaries, or provide a statement of beneficiaries where ultimate beneficiaries remain unascertained. This confirmation is notarised and kept in the private records of the resident agent; it is not publicly registered unless the foundation has waived confidentiality.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Registry of Foundation Charter and By-laws
Minute Book of Foundation Council Resolutions
Register of Beneficial Owners maintained by the resident agent under Law 23 of 2015
Register of Notarial Alterations and Amending Documents

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250 - USD 650 for a standard PIF with registered office and licensed resident-agent compliance services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 - USD 6,000 only if the foundation becomes a global relevant taxpayer or its governing instrument requires a certified audit; a non-audited PIF incurs no mandatory audit fee

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% flat on net taxable income of Panamanian source; foreign-source income is exempt under the territorial system
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territoriality (0% on foreign-source income); Private Interest Foundation passive patrimony exemption (Ley 25 de 1995, Art. 47); Multinational Headquarters (SEM, Ley 41 de 2007) 5% on qualifying international services; Free Zone and Panama Pacífico regimes (full or partial ISR exemption)
